label: Epipolar Geometry and the Fundamental Matrix
notes: This chapter, printed pages 239 to 261, opens the two-view story. Two cameras looking at one scene share a rigid geometry that is independent of the scene structure. Our goal is to read the fundamental matrix as the algebraic machine that encodes that geometry, turning correspondence search into a search along a single line.

label: The Two-View Setup
notes: Set the stage carefully: two camera centers, the baseline joining them, and a 3D point seen by both. The three points define an epipolar plane, and the matter of correspondence is entirely controlled by this triangle. Everything algebraic that follows is a coordinate shadow of this one picture, so spend time on it.

label: Epipoles, Planes, and Lines
notes: Name the actors. The epipole in each image is where the baseline pierces that image plane, equivalently the projection of the other camera centre. Every epipolar plane contains the baseline, so every epipolar line passes through the epipole. The pencil of planes about the baseline maps to a pencil of lines through the epipole.

label: The Fundamental Matrix Defined
notes: Now the algebra. The fundamental matrix is the unique three by three homogeneous matrix satisfying the incidence relation for every corresponding pair. It is the algebraic shadow of the epipolar plane. Stress that it is homogeneous, so only its ratios matter, and that it is defined purely by the two cameras, not the scene.

label: Point Maps to Epipolar Line
notes: This is the workhorse identity. Multiplying a point in the first image by F yields the coefficients of a line in the second image. The corresponding point must lie on that line. Emphasise that F is a correlation, mapping points to lines rather than points to points, which is why correspondence reduces to a line search.

label: Rank Two and Seven Degrees of Freedom
notes: Two structural facts pin F down. It has rank two, so its determinant vanishes and it has a one-dimensional null space. Counting nine entries, minus overall scale, minus the rank-two constraint, leaves seven degrees of freedom. Both facts are essential when estimating F from correspondences, since a full-rank estimate is wrong.

label: Epipoles as Null Vectors
notes: The epipoles re-enter algebraically. The right epipole is the right null vector of F, the left epipole the left null vector. This is exactly why epipolar lines all meet at the epipole: every line F x contains e prime. The notebook verified these null residuals down to machine precision, confirming the geometry.

label: F from the Camera Matrices
notes: Connect F back to the cameras. Given the two projection matrices, F is the cross-product matrix of the second epipole times the second camera times the pseudo-inverse of the first. This formula shows F is computable directly from calibration, and it makes transparent why the second epipole appears as a left null vector.

label: The Essential Matrix
notes: Calibration sharpens the story. Pre-multiplying by the two intrinsic matrices converts F into the essential matrix, which acts on normalised image coordinates. E equals the translation cross-product times the rotation, so it carries the metric motion. Its signature is two equal nonzero singular values and one zero, stricter than a generic rank-two matrix.

label: Special Motions
notes: Special motions test understanding. Pure lateral translation sends the epipole to infinity, so the epipolar lines become parallel rather than meeting at a finite point. Forward motion places the epipole near the image centre. Crucially, the rank-two contract survives as long as the two camera centres remain distinct.

label: Correspondence Along a Line
notes: Here is the payoff for stereo. Instead of scanning a whole image for a match, you scan one epipolar line predicted by F. This collapses a two-dimensional search to one dimension, the foundation of rectified stereo and the practical reason epipolar geometry matters in reconstruction pipelines.

label: Synthesis and Checks
notes: Close by tying the picture to numbers. The notebook built a calibrated rig, confirmed rank two, verified epipoles as null vectors, checked the incidence residual at machine precision, and recovered the equal-singular-value signature of E. Carry forward that F is geometry encoded algebraically, ready for estimation in the next chapter.
